newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Court clears BA plan for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Court clears BA plan for Air Liberte.

text.p: British Airways won court approval on Thursday to acquire insolvent carrier Air Liberte and expand its presence in the French air travel market to more than 20 percent.

The president of the Creteil commercial court, Dominique Leveque, said the court agreed to the plan presented by BA and its French partner Banque Rivaud to take control of Air Liberte and invest 780 million francs ($147 million) to keep the carrier in the air.
Although the French industry and government were initially reluctant to allow Air Liberte to fall into foreign hands, Leveque said there was no "acceptable alternative plan".
Richard Branson's Virgin Express had said it might put in a bid but declined last month.

With the ruling, BA will control 67 percent of Air Liberte, and Rivaud, which had been the biggest shareholder in Air Liberte before it went into receivership, will have 28 percent. Minority shareholders will retain five percent.
"This is excellent news, not just for Air Liberte and its employees but also for French travellers," BA chief executive Bob Ayling said in a statement.

"With the financial backing of British Airways and the Rivaud group and our expertise in cost control, yield management and client services, Air Liberte will recover the position it deserves in the French market," he said.

The court ruling confirmed a takeover that had already begun. Air Liberte's board last month elected the head of BA's French subsidiary TAT, Marc Rochet, as its chairman, and the two partners have started pouring cash into Air Liberte.
BA has said it plans eventually to merge Air Liberte and TAT, which jointly hold 22 percent of the market dominated by Air France's regional arm Air France Europe.
BA's aim is to restore Air Liberte and TAT to profitability in three years.
Air Liberte lost 650 million francs in the 12 months to October after a price war broke out in the French market following its liberalisation at the start of 1996.

BA and Rivaud, which initially backed rival bids for the carrier, joined forces in October to present a recovery plan to avoid liquidation of Air Liberte, which had gone into receivership the previous month.
The rescue plan offers creditors owed a total of 1.5 billion francs two options -- 20 percent in cash within a year or the full amount over 10 years.
French newspapers reported that many creditors appeared to be confident of the carrier's recovery and were opting for the entire amount over a 10-year period.
BA has said it plans to retain 1,249 of the 1,400 jobs at Air Liberte.

BA and Rivaud have invested 150 million francs in the carrier -- BA put in 100 million and Rivaud 50 million. BA will invest a further 440 million and Rivaud will add 190 million, the British carrier said in its statement.
